codex.variables.name: Variables
codex.variables.happened: The attack was {expression}. With your numbers filled in: {filled} = {value}.
codex.identifiers.name: Identifiers
codex.identifiers.happened: You tried to reach {real} as {name}, and C# refused. A name starts with a letter or _, holds only letters, digits and _, and is never a keyword like class. Capitals count: Shadow is a different name from shadow.
codex.int-truncation.name: Integer truncation
codex.int-truncation.happened: {before} damage hit {enemy:target}, an int. An int has no room for decimals, so they were cut off: {after}.
codex.integer-division.name: Integer division
codex.integer-division.happened: {expression} gave {value}. When both sides are int, C# throws the remainder away: 7 / 2 is 3, not 3.5.
codex.modulo.name: Modulo
codex.modulo.happened: {expression} gave {value}. % gives what is left after dividing: 7 % 3 is 1. The rest is always smaller than the number you divide by, so cards % 3 == 0 is true on every third card.
codex.increment.name: ++ and --
codex.increment.happened: {expression} gave {value}, and afterwards the counter was {after}. count++ hands out the old value and then adds 1. ++count adds 1 first and hands out the new value.
codex.booleans.name: Booleans
codex.booleans.happened: {expression} became {value}. A bool has only two values, true and false, and ! flips it. Flip it twice and you are back where you started.
codex.overflow.name: Integer overflow
codex.overflow.happened: {enemy:target} was a {type} with {before} HP. Adding {added} made it {after}: a {type} can't go past {max}, so it wrapped around.
codex.operator-precedence.name: Operator precedence
codex.operator-precedence.happened: {expression} is {value}. *, / and % go before + and -, and brackets go first of all. Move the brackets, and the same numbers give another answer.
codex.constants.name: Constants
codex.constants.happened: {expression} didn't compile: the attack was const. A constant gets its value once, and nobody can assign it again.
codex.string-concat.name: String concatenation
codex.string-concat.happened: {expression} became {value}. With text, + glues instead of adding.
codex.string-length.name: String length
codex.string-length.happened: The text was {length} characters long. Every character counts: "6" is one, "2.5" is three, and a space counts too.
codex.char-is-number.name: A char is a number
codex.char-is-number.happened: {expression} gave {value}. Every char is a number: 'A' is 65, and the character '0' is 48, not 0.
codex.casting.name: Casting
codex.casting.happened: You remolded {enemy:target} from {from} to {to}: {before} became {after}. Remolding has a real name: casting.
codex.convert.name: Convert
codex.convert.happened: {expression} gave {value}. Convert rounds .5 to the nearest even number, and it checks: if a value doesn't fit, your program crashes instead of wrapping.
codex.rounding.name: Math.Round
codex.rounding.happened: {before} damage on {enemy:enemy} became {after}. Math.Round sends .5 to the nearest even number: 2.5 is 2, 3.5 is 4.
codex.parse.name: Parsing
codex.parse.happened: {text} gave {value}. Text that looks like a number is still text, until you parse it.
codex.exceptions.name: Exceptions
codex.exceptions.happened: {expression} threw a {exception}. The code compiled fine, but crashed while it ran.
bug.golem.title: Pac-Man, level 256 (1980)
bug.golem.story: Pac-Man kept the level number in a single byte. After level 255 came 256, which a byte cannot hold. The game drew half the maze from garbage memory, and nobody could finish it.
bug.effective-power.title: Effective Power (iPhone, 2015)
bug.effective-power.story: One text message could crash any iPhone that received it. It held a short run of Arabic and other Unicode characters that the phone's text layout couldn't handle. The moment the message appeared in a notification, the phone tried to draw it and crashed, over and over. This one crashes too, once its text gets long enough.
bug.y2k.title: Y2K (1999)
bug.y2k.story: To save space, old programs kept only the last two digits of a year. Many websites then wrote the date as "19" + (year - 1900). That worked for a century. On 1 January 2000 the year minus 1900 was 100, and pages proudly showed the year 19100. This one rewrites its year every turn, so whatever you glued onto it is gone. Make it long enough within one turn, and it crashes.
bug.counter.title: Gangnam Style (YouTube, 2014)
bug.counter.story: YouTube counted views in a 32-bit int. Gangnam Style got so popular that its counter crept toward 2,147,483,647, the largest number an int can hold. One more and it would have wrapped around to minus two billion. YouTube switched to a 64-bit counter just in time. This counter wasn't so lucky.
bug.colossus.title: Ariane 5, flight 501 (1996)
bug.colossus.story: Ariane 5 reused software from the smaller Ariane 4. A speed value that fit fine on the old rocket was too large for its new, smaller type. The conversion failed, the guidance shut down, and the rocket destroyed itself 37 seconds after launch.
bug.index.title: Vancouver Stock Exchange (1982)
bug.index.story: A new stock index started at 1000. It was recalculated thousands of times a day, and every time the result was cut off after three decimals instead of rounded. Each cut lost a tiny bit. After 22 months the index stood at about 520, while its real value was over 1000.

ui.subtitle: Act 1: The Vat Valley
ui.tagline: A deckbuilder where the world obeys C#.
ui.intro.title: Not by the manual
ui.intro.1: The factory builds everything by the specification. You are the little figure from its assembly manual.
ui.intro.2: The manual is full of crossed-out panels: things you must never do. But the manual is only paper. The world obeys C#, and C# allows a lot more.
ui.intro.3: Nobody will explain the rules. Bump into them, bend them, break them. The Codex will tell you their names later.

bug.goto-fail.title: goto fail; (Apple, 2014)
bug.goto-fail.story: For about eighteen months, iPhones and Macs could be fooled by fake secure connections. In Apple's code, one line was accidentally there twice: goto fail; The copy had no condition, so it always ran, and the most important check below it was skipped. Nobody noticed, because the code still looked like it checked everything. This automaton has the same mistake: rule 3 is a copy of rule 2 without its condition.
bug.knight-capital.title: Knight Capital (2012)
bug.knight-capital.story: Knight Capital bought and sold shares automatically. Its code still held an old feature, Power Peg, that nobody had used in years. During an update, the flag that used to switch Power Peg on got a new meaning, but one server never received the new code. There, the old rule was suddenly reached again. In 45 minutes the system placed millions of orders, and the company lost 440 million dollars. This automaton has the same old rule at the top: once it's reached, it does nothing else.

bug.day-248.title: Boeing 787 (2015)
bug.day-248.story: In 2015 Boeing found that a counter in the 787's power control overflowed once the plane had been powered on for 248 days straight. All generators would then switch to a safe mode at the same time, and the whole aircraft would lose power, even in flight. It never happened: the aviation authority required the planes to be fully switched off regularly until the software was fixed. This automaton counts too, and its only rule looks at that counter.

belt.level.first-belt.brief: Tin Knights. Each knight gets 5 HP more before it leaves for the front.
belt.level.double-up.name: Doubling
belt.level.double-up.brief: Slime Blobs, each with at least 30 HP. Double them until they get there: how often depends on what comes in.
belt.level.three-times.name: Three times
belt.level.three-times.brief: Bottomless Jugs with exactly 12 HP extra. You only have one +4 and one +6.
belt.level.at-least-once.name: At least once
belt.level.at-least-once.brief: Drippers: +3 at least once, then again until they have at least 10 HP.
belt.level.nested.name: Loop in a loop
belt.level.nested.brief: Floating Ghosts with 24 HP extra. You only have a +1, and a counter counts to 6 at most.
belt.level.round-up.name: Rounding up
belt.level.round-up.brief: Rhythm Turtles march in rows of 5: round their HP up to a multiple of 5. What already fits, stays.
belt.level.byte-loop.name: Laps in a byte
belt.level.byte-loop.brief: Level 256 cabinets. Their HP is a byte. Add 20 as long as it's more than 100.
belt.level.halving.name: Halving
belt.level.halving.brief: Splitters: halve their HP until it's 5 at most. Their HP is an int.
belt.level.padding.name: Padding
belt.level.padding.brief: Labels for the front: pad with dashes until the text is 6 characters long. What's long enough already, stays.
belt.level.zune.name: Zune
belt.level.zune.brief: This loop turns a number of days into the day of the year, in a leap year. It works, except on one day. Find that day, and give it a way out.
codex.while-loop.name: while and do while
codex.while-loop.happened: Your gate ({condition}) saw the same product {passes} times: the belt ran back to the gate. As long as the condition is true, the product goes around again. With the gate before the work, it's a while; with the gate after it, a do while, which always works at least once.
codex.for-loop.name: for
codex.for-loop.happened: Your counter sent the product into the loop {times} times, then let it through. Repeating a fixed number of times: that's a for. Afterwards the counter starts at 0 again.
codex.nested-loops.name: Nested loops
codex.nested-loops.happened: A counter of {inner} ran inside a counter of {outer}: {outer} times {inner} is {total} laps. A loop in a loop.
codex.infinite-loop.name: Infinite loop
codex.infinite-loop.happened: After {ticks} ticks, everything was exactly as before: the product ({value}) on the same square, with the same contents. From then on, everything repeats, forever. The condition to stop never becomes true.
xpanel.belt-forever.name: Never let the belt run forever
xpanel.belt-forever.text: A product never left the belt: an infinite loop.
xpanel.conveyor-cleared.name: Do not stop at chapter 6
xpanel.conveyor-cleared.text: You delivered the last order of the Conveyor Belt.
xpanel.dropped-crate.name: Drop nothing off the belt
xpanel.dropped-crate.text: A product fell off the belt, onto a square without belt.
bug.zune.title: Zune (2008)
bug.zune.story: On 31 December 2008, every Microsoft Zune 30 music player froze at the same time when starting up. Its clock turned a number of days into a year and a day, in a while loop. In a leap year, the loop only took off a year if more than 366 days were left. On day 366 of 2008, nothing happened, and the loop ran forever. The fix: wait until the battery ran out, and try again after midnight.
